ca_mama_cat_boulder.blurb: A compact bouldering spot in Woodfords Canyon, alongside the Carson Pass highway south of Lake Tahoe, at roughly 5,800 feet. Twelve problems sit on the main Mama Cat boulder, with a single line on the small Mama Kitten boulder beside it. The range is wide for so few problems: a couple of easy warm-ups, then a solid middle of V2 to V6, and one problem up around V8. A couple of the face and arete lines are rated as committing, so bring enough pads and a spotter. It makes a handy short stop for a climber already in the canyon rather than a destination on its own.

ca_peyote_cracks_formation_w_face.blurb: The west-facing side of a stand-alone formation in the Outback of Joshua Tree, near Echo Cove. The wall is close to vertical and cut by several cracks, led by three main splitters that run from easy to a stiff 5.10 or 5.11. Climbs are short, with the hard moves low down, so they get soloed as often as they are led. Most of the thirteen routes are trad, a few are easy to set up as top-ropes, and there is one V3 boulder problem. Grades spread from beginner terrain to 5.11, with the bulk at 5.10 and 5.11. Expect afternoon sun on the face.
ca_peyote_cracks_formation_w_face.parking_note: Leave the car in the back loop of Hidden Valley Campground and walk north toward Echo Cove, or park at Echo Cove and take the old road southwest, then a climber path.

ca_mid_dome.blurb: A tall slab dome of about 250 feet above the Echo Lakes basin near Echo Summit, south of Lake Tahoe. The surface is mostly low-angle and fine-featured, with a few steeper pockets and the odd crack; the face points south, so it catches the sun for most of the day and can get hot and polished underfoot. Thirteen routes split between bolted lines, trad lines and one top-rope, from an easy 5.7 up through a core of 5.10 and 5.11 to a single 5.12. Several of the bolted lines are spaced far apart, so lead them with care. Every route finishes with a walk-off down a loose gully on the northwest side.

ca_lieback_rock.blurb: One of the boulders in the Moby Dick Area of the Santee Boulders, in San Diego County. It is the northernmost boulder of the group, usually well chalked, and easy to recognise by a prominent edge on the right side of its main face. To find it, go over the crest of the hill from the Painted Crack Boulder; it is the last boulder on the right, just beyond the Mudball Cracks. The thirteen problems are mostly short and friendly, from easy mantles, slabs and a crack through to V3 lines and traverses, plus a few far harder problems. Grades for several lines are debated, so treat them loosely.

ca_ghost_town_a_k_a_windermere.blurb: A small, quiet bouldering area in the forest above Santa Barbara, at around 2,100 feet. The climbing centres on three to five large boulders, roughly 15 to 20 feet tall, and the tree canopy keeps them shaded, so the rock stays cool; mornings and late afternoons feel best. Thirteen problems range from V1 warm-ups to a few V7 to V9 testpieces, with most falling between V1 and V5. The style leans technical and friction-based rather than powerful. It rarely gets busy, but the rock is slow to dry, so skip it after rain. Bring pads and a brush, and keep noise down.

ca_north_astro_dome_northeast_face.blurb: The northeast side of North Astro Dome, a big, steep formation at the western edge of Wonderland Valley in Joshua Tree. Climbs run from one to four pitches, mostly trad, with one top-rope and a single boulder problem, and the stone is regarded as excellent. Grades go from 5.7 up to 5.12, with the best lines at 5.10 and harder. Expect thin edging on tiny holds, with bolts that are spaced far apart, so a small rack is useful. Because the face looks northeast it sees little sun and feels cold in winter; a warm January day suits it. Descent is by rappel from anchors on top.
